response.rationale: Periorbital induration with scleritis and histopathology showing necrobiotic granulomatous inflammation, abundant mucin, and giant cells is characteristic of necrobiotic xanthogranuloma; negative infection/malignancy stains and absence of foreign material or non-caseating sarcoid granulomas favor it over alternatives.

rejected.why: Granulomatous inflammation is nonspecific; idiopathic orbital inflammatory disease would not typically show central necrobiosis and extensive mucin, and the lesion was painless and stable rather than acutely inflamed.
Sarcoidosis classically shows non-necrotizing granulomas without central necrobiosis or mucin, and no systemic sarcoid features are provided.
Recent surgery is a distractor; foreign body granuloma would show foreign material or foreign-body giant cells, not necrobiosis and Alcian-blue-positive mucin.
